#### ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

### attrition dataset: data exploration and necessary cleaning

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)   
tidymodels_prefer()   

attrition <- read_csv("attrition.csv")   # load dataset

```

```{r}
# check types of features
# you will notice a lot <chr> character features, we will need to convert them into <fct> for modeling (see below)

glimpse(attrition)

```


```{r}
# convert all character variables to factor variables if required

attrition <- attrition |> mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor))

glimpse(attrition)   # all <chr> converted to <fct>

```


```{r}
# check for missing entries, which features have missing entries?
# distribution of features

library(skimr)

skim(attrition)

```


```{r}
# verify the levels of every factor-type feature

attrition |>
  select(where(is.factor)) |>
  map(levels)

```


```{r}
# make "Yes" (employee leaves) the first level, i.e., the event of interest
# this is for modeling and calculating performance metrics later

attrition <- attrition |>
  mutate(Attrition = fct_relevel(Attrition, "Yes"))

levels(attrition$Attrition)

```


```{r}
# imbalanced dataset in terms of response classes

attrition |>
  count(Attrition) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n))

```



#### ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

### attrition dataset: data splitting

```{r}
# split original data into training (60%), validation (20%), and test (20%) sets
# stratify on the response so each set keeps the ~16% attrition rate

set.seed(208)

attrition_split <- initial_validation_split(data = attrition,
                                            prop = c(0.6, 0.2),
                                            strata = Attrition)

attrition_train <- training(attrition_split)        # training set
attrition_validation <- validation(attrition_split) # validation set
attrition_test <- testing(attrition_split)          # test set

```


```{r}
# verify even distribution of response classes across the three sets

bind_rows(train = attrition_train,
          validation = attrition_validation,
          test = attrition_test,
          .id = "set") |>
  count(set, Attrition) |>
  group_by(set) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n))

```


### check for zv/nzv features

```{r}
# check for zv/nzv features in training set

library(caret)

nearZeroVar(attrition_train, saveMetrics = TRUE)

```
